findings.description: The bucket is documented in-code as public and has no ACL restriction, no bucket policy, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so public ACLs/policies can be applied and the bucket contents (including a customer master file) can be exposed to anonymous internet users.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/customer-managed key encryption.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this sensitive bucket produces no S3 server access audit trail, hindering detection and investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted (maliciously or accidentally) cannot be recovered, weakening integrity protection for the stored data.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in unencrypted public bucket
findings.description: A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded from the repository into the publicly exposed, unencrypted aws_s3_bucket.data with no kms_key_id set, placing confidential customer records in a world-readable, unencrypted location (and committing it to version control).
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest using a customer-managed KMS key.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial data, leaving no audit trail of object-level access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so deletion or tampering with financial objects is irreversible and undetectable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could make this financial data publicly readable without any account-level guardrail preventing it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so data in the operations bucket is not encrypted with a managed KMS key by default.
Server access logging is not configured, so access to the bucket is not auditable.
The bucket lacks an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing prevents public ACLs or policies from being applied later.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving potentially sensitive analytical datasets unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so account-level public exposure guardrails are absent.
The audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a subsequent ACL or policy change could expose access logs (which reveal request patterns and principals) publicly.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached, so log data may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
